content: What do folks think about having a blueprint for CSLib?

I was also wondering why this was never established for such projects (think mathlib).

I would indeed be interested to perhaps see some connections, while also (me personally) not being forced to remove my annotations (think leanarchitect) of private blueprint projects before merging into cslib.

The pattern that very successful emerged for Mathlib was having blueprints happen downstream, then during/afterwards upsteaming reusable portions. Maybe it'd also be fine to to have these within CSLib itself though, as we are much younger and have less of a Bourbaki-like style. I would probably choose the Verso variant of blueprints for maintainability reasons. If there's a blueprint anyone already has in mind, I would welcome a first try at this!

(But please human-written for this sort of thing, I don't think an LLM will do well here)

Chris Anto Fröschl said:

think mathlib

AFAIK the opinions between maintainers vary too wildly to be able to agree on a blueprint, but there are project boards

Yes, to be clear I was advocating for blueprints for any individual points of interest, not dictating the direction of CSLib. I think blueprints leading up to some big theorem are nice in terms of collaboration.
Is there an example blueprint I can take a look at?

I am actually interested in having a blueprint which documents the intended direction of CSLib where we actually collaboratively construct the path forward. That way we can do much farther out thinking than the current PR when we're doing these reviews, cause we can be expanding/changing the blueprint as we go. Here is the blueprint for complexitylib which I use as a part of the roadmap tracking strategy: https://samuelschlesinger.github.io/complexitylib/blueprint/. Heavily AI authored, against Chris' earlier desire, so it would be an interesting case study to see if it turned out terribly. For me, I find it very helpful for navigation of the high-level mathematical content compared to the Lean docs UI or my text editor.

I see. I'm not inherently opposed to having a wider blueprint of milestones (ultimately it will still be up to individuals to implement), but I would push back very hard on it being AI-written. The point of a blueprint in my view is to communicate and coordinate human intent to formalize. If it's something else, it doesn't need to be committed to the library.
Happy to have a line in our contribution guide restricting it to human authorship.
If the purpose is to set milestones as opposed to expressing what’s already in the library, then I don’t see the point of a blueprint over the already existing README files.
Blueprints add something when they add informal text explaining formal theorems, definitions, and proofs.
That's what I want it for, but yes the current READMEs satisfy this need as well.
